definitions.explanation: A designated place where buses pick up and drop off passengers.

examples.japanese: バス{停|てい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。
examples.english: To wait at the bus stop.

examples.japanese: ⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧バス{停|てい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{降|お}りる→降りる：00568_oriru⟧。
examples.english: To get off at the next bus stop.
The bus stop is in front of the station.

notes:
A contraction of ⟦バス→バス：00769_basu⟧⟦{停留所|ていりゅうじょ}→停留所：03440_teiryuujo⟧ (bus stop — full formal term). バス{停|てい} is the standard everyday form.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- バス{停|てい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧: to wait at the bus stop
- バス{停|てい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{降|お}りる→降りる：00568_oriru⟧: to get off at the bus stop
- ⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧バス{停|てい}: the next bus stop
- ⟦{最寄|もよ}り→最寄り：28821_moyori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧バス{停|てい}: the nearest bus stop

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{停留所|ていりゅうじょ}→停留所：03440_teiryuujo⟧: bus stop (formal, used on maps and official signs)
- ⟦バス→バス：00769_basu⟧⟦{乗|の}り{場|ば}→乗り場：01041_noriba⟧: bus boarding area (at larger stations or terminals)
- ⟦バス→バス：00769_basu⟧⟦ターミナル→ターミナル：11037_taaminaru⟧: bus terminal

In Japanese cities, bus stops typically display route maps, timetables, and the stop name. The formal name ⟦{停留所|ていりゅうじょ}→停留所：03440_teiryuujo⟧ appears on official signs, but people say バス{停|てい} in conversation.
